questions.q: The tsconfig has "rootDir": "src" and "outDir": "dist". You run npx tsc. Where does src/lib/store.ts end up?
questions.explain: rootDir says where the .ts files are, and the folder structure inside it is copied to outDir. So src/lib/store.ts becomes dist/lib/store.js.

questions.q: In this project, what is the difference between npx tsc --noEmit and npx tsc?
questions.explain: With --noEmit, tsc reports errors and writes nothing. Without it, tsc also builds the project into outDir. That is why the check script is tsc --noEmit and the build script is tsc.
options: --noEmit only checks the types; plain tsc checks and also writes the .js files to dist/
--noEmit skips the type check; plain tsc only checks

questions.q: With verbatimModuleSyntax on, what does TypeScript do with imports when it compiles a file?
questions.explain: One simple rule: import type disappears, everything else stays. No guessing means every tool (tsc, tsx, Node.js, the browser terminal) agrees on what is removed.
options: It guesses which imports are only types and removes them
It removes every import type, and keeps every other import exactly as written
It removes all imports and bundles the files together

questions.q: task.ts exports the value STATUSES and the interface Task. tsc reports TS1484 on import { STATUSES, Task } from "./task.js";. Which line fixes it?
questions.explain: Mark just the type with type inside the braces. import type for both would remove STATUSES too, and it is a real value you use at runtime.

questions.q: tsx does not check types. In the lesson's project, whose tsconfig has verbatimModuleSyntax on, what happens when you run npx tsx src/oops.ts, where the file starts with import { STATUSES, Task } from "./task.js"; and Task is an interface?
questions.explain: Interfaces are erased, so the running task.js has no Task export. tsx reads verbatimModuleSyntax from the tsconfig, so it keeps the normal import exactly as written, Node.js asks for Task, and throws a SyntaxError. (Without that setting, tsx would guess and drop the unused name, and the program would run.) TS1484 is the type checker catching this first; tsx never shows TS errors.
options: It runs fine, because tsx removes Task automatically
It crashes: the module ./task.js does not provide an export named Task
It prints a warning and sets Task to undefined

questions.q: What does tsc say about this file?
questions.explain: An import type is removed before the code runs, so anything imported that way may only be used as a type. A value like STATUSES needs a normal import (TS1361).
options: Nothing: import type works for values too
An error: STATUSES cannot be used as a value because it was imported with import type
An error: the path must end in .ts

questions.q: With verbatimModuleSyntax on, as in the lesson's project, which line of this barrel file (index.ts) does tsc reject? Task and Status are types, STATUSES is a value.
questions.explain: Re-exporting a type needs export type, for the same reason importing one needs import type (TS1205: "Re-exporting a type when 'verbatimModuleSyntax' is enabled requires using 'export type'"). Values like STATUSES use a normal export.

questions.q: What belongs in a barrel file (index.ts)?
questions.explain: A barrel gives other code one place to import from, so it does not need to know which file each function lives in. It contains only export … from lines. Every ZudoJS package is built this way.
options: The main program logic, so it runs first
Only re-exports of the folder's public parts, never logic
Every type in the project, copied in one place
The tsconfig settings for the folder

questions.q: The file is src/store.ts. Why does main.ts import it as "./store.js"?
questions.explain: tsc removes types and leaves the rest as written, so the import path goes into dist/main.js unchanged. There, the file next to it is store.js. When checking, tsc knows ./store.js will be built from ./store.ts and reads that file's types.
options: Because TypeScript rewrites .js to .ts when it runs
Because TypeScript never changes import paths: you write the path of the file that will run, dist/store.js
Because .ts files can only be imported by .js files
It is a style choice; "./store" works the same

questions.q: With NodeNext, what does tsc say about import { addTask } from "./store";?
questions.explain: Node's ES modules never guess file extensions, and NodeNext follows Node's rules, so TypeScript does not guess either. The error message even suggests the fix.
options: Error TS2835: relative imports need an explicit file extension, did you mean "./store.js"?
It works in tsc but fails in tsx

questions.q: What is the problem with import { board } from "./format.ts"; in this project?
questions.explain: Import paths are copied unchanged into the output, and dist/ only has .js files. tsc stops you (TS5097) unless you turn on special settings. The course, like ZudoJS, writes .js.
options: Nothing, it is the recommended style
TypeScript cannot read .ts files through an import
The built dist/main.js would import format.ts, a file that does not exist in dist/

questions.q: The folder src/tasks/ has an index.ts barrel. Which import is correct with NodeNext?
questions.explain: In ES modules a folder name alone does not load its index.js, and extensions are never guessed. Write the full path of the file that will run: ./tasks/index.js.

questions.q: With "moduleResolution": "NodeNext", how is import { schema } from "@zudojs/schema" found?
questions.explain: Only paths starting with ./ or ../ are files next to the current one. Anything else is a package in node_modules, and its package.json says which file to load.
options: As a file called @zudojs/schema.ts next to the current file
As a package in node_modules, through its package.json
It is downloaded from npm when the program starts
TypeScript searches every folder of the project for it

questions.q: After someone removes "type": "module" from package.json, npx tsc --noEmit shows fifteen TS1295 errors about import in a CommonJS file. What is the fix?
questions.explain: Without "type": "module", Node.js treats .js files as CommonJS, so TypeScript does too, and import/export are not allowed. Many errors, one fix. When you see TS1295 or TS1287, check package.json first.

questions.q: package.json has "type": "module". Which file is still treated as CommonJS?
questions.explain: The nearest package.json decides for .ts and .js files. The extensions .mts (ES module) and .cts (CommonJS) force one or the other, whatever package.json says.

questions.q: A package's package.json has "exports": { ".": { "types": "./dist/index.d.ts", "import": "./dist/index.js" } }. What is "types" for?
questions.explain: "types" points TypeScript to the .d.ts declaration file, which holds only types. "import" is the JavaScript file Node.js runs for an import. "." means the package's main entry.
options: It is the file Node.js runs
It is the declaration file TypeScript reads for the package's types
It lists the TypeScript version the package needs
It is the file tsc compiles when you install the package

questions.q: Why is import { schema } from "@zudojs/schema/dist/schemaRoot/index.js" refused by tsc and by Node.js, even though the file is in node_modules?
questions.explain: Only what "exports" lists is public. Node.js throws ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED and tsc cannot find the module. That lets authors reorganise internal files without breaking you. Import from the package name.
options: Because that path is not listed in the package's "exports", so it is private to the package
Because node_modules files cannot be imported with .js

questions.q: The project has the scripts check, build, start (node dist/main.js) and dev (tsx src/main.ts). What does a server run in production?
questions.explain: dev is for working on your machine. Before shipping you check and build; in production, start runs the compiled JavaScript in dist/.
options: npm run dev, because it needs no build
npm run build once, then npm start to run the built JavaScript
npm run check, which also starts the server

questions.q: Should the dist/ folder be committed to Git?
questions.explain: dist/ is built from src/ every time, so it does not belong in the repository. Anyone can recreate it with npm run build.
options: Yes, so other people do not need TypeScript
No: it is generated by npm run build, so add it to .gitignore
No, because Git cannot store .js files

questions.q: Infer is a type exported by @zudojs/schema. What does this print?
questions.explain: schema is a real value in the running package; Infer is only a type, so it does not exist at runtime. Marking it type Infer in the import makes it disappear, so nothing asks for a missing export.
options: SyntaxError: The requested module does not provide an export named 'Infer'

questions.explain: Record<Status, number> requires a number for every status, so the counts start as { todo: 0, doing: 0, done: 0 }. doing stays 0 but is still printed.

questions.explain: readonly string[] only stops the caller from changing the array through that type. It is still the same array, so it sees the two tasks added later. readonly is a type; it does not copy anything.

questions.explain: STATUSES is a real value that exists at runtime, unlike the Status type. Reading methods like map, includes and indexOf work on a readonly array. Indexes start at 0, so "done" is at 2.

questions.q: A type and a value may share a name. What does this print?
questions.explain: After the types are erased, only the value Book (a schema object) is left, so typeof Book is "object". The type Book is used only in the annotation Book[], which disappears.

questions.q: This code reads a package's package.json like Node.js does. What does it print?
questions.explain: "import" is the file Node.js runs, "types" the one TypeScript reads. A deep path is not listed under "exports", so there is nothing to find: that is why a deep import is refused.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: You export a type exactly like a value, but only the value DEFAULT_STATUS exists when the program runs. The object is plain data; the Task interface leaves no trace in it.

questions.q: @zudojs/schema exports schema (a value) and SchemaResult (a type). What does this print?
questions.explain: import type for SchemaResult is removed before the code runs, so nothing asks the package for it. safeParse returns a result object instead of throwing, and 42 is not a string.
options: SyntaxError: The requested module does not provide an export named 'SchemaResult'

questions.q: A relative import is resolved against the file that runs it. URL follows the same rule. What does this print?
questions.explain: ./ means the folder of the current file and ../ goes one folder up. At runtime the current file is in dist/, so the import must name a .js file that exists there.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: This is what rootDir: "src" and outDir: "dist" do: the folders inside src/ are kept, and each .ts file becomes a .js file under dist/.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A module namespace object holds only the values the package really exports at runtime. SchemaIssue is a type, so it is not there, which is exactly why it must be imported with import type.

questions.q: Finish countByStatus. It returns a Record<Status, number> with a count for every status, including the ones with no tasks. The program should print { todo: 1, doing: 1, done: 2 }.
questions.explain: Start every status at 0, in the order you want them printed, then add one per task. Record<Status, number> makes TypeScript complain if you forget a status in the starting object.

questions.q: This program crashes when run: Infer is a type, but it is imported like a value. Fix only the import line, the way the lesson teaches, so the program prints Buy milk.
questions.explain: Write type in front of Infer inside the braces. Then the type is removed before the code runs, and schema, a real value, is still imported. import type { schema, Infer } would remove schema too.

questions.q:
Write outPath(file), which works out where tsc writes a file with "rootDir": "src" and "outDir": "dist": replace the leading src/ with dist/ and the ending .ts with .js. The program should print:

dist/main.js
dist/lib/store.js
questions.explain: The folder structure inside rootDir is copied to outDir, so lib/ stays. Only the root folder and the extension change. This is also why imports say .js: that is the name the file has in dist/.

questions.q: Write importKind(specifier) using NodeNext's rule: a specifier starting with ./ or ../ is a "file"; anything else is a "package". The program should print [ 'file', 'file', 'package', 'package' ].
questions.explain: Relative paths point at a file next to the current one. Everything else, scoped like @zudojs/schema or not, is looked up in node_modules through the package's package.json.

questions.q:
Write fixSpecifier(spec), which turns a relative import into the form NodeNext wants. Relative paths (starting with .) that end in .ts get .js instead; relative paths with no .js ending get .js added. Package names stay as they are. The program should print:

./store.js
./format.js
./task.js
@zudojs/schema
questions.explain: With NodeNext, a relative import names the file that will run, .js included. "./store" is TS2835 and "./format.ts" is TS5097; both become .js. A package name is resolved through node_modules, so it is left alone.

questions.q: Write moduleFormat(file, packageType): files ending in .mts are "esm" and files ending in .cts are "commonjs", whatever the package says. Other files are "esm" when packageType is "module", otherwise "commonjs". The program should print esm commonjs esm commonjs.
questions.explain: The last case is the "missing "type": "module"" bug from the lesson: without it, every .ts/.js file is CommonJS, and import/export are rejected (TS1295).

questions.q:
Write resolveImport(exportsField, subpath) the way Node.js reads "exports": return the import file listed for the subpath, or throw an Error with the message ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED when the subpath is not listed. The program should print:

./dist/index.js
ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED
questions.explain: Only listed subpaths are public; "." is the main entry. Anything else is private, even if the file exists in node_modules. Node.js uses the "import" file, and TypeScript the "types" file.

questions.q:
Finish board(tasks). It returns one line per status, in the order of STATUSES, like todo: A, B. When a status has no tasks, show -. The program should print:

todo: -
doing: Call Ada
done: Buy milk, Pay rent
questions.explain: Loop over STATUSES (a real value), not over the tasks, so every status gets a line in a fixed order. An empty join gives "", and || "-" replaces it.
